output_contract_strategy.stdout_strategy: JSON-only stdout; future runner refactors must not introduce stray prints; golden cases assert json.loads(stdout) succeeds and that subset of locked fields equals expected literals.
output_contract_strategy.stderr_strategy: empty by default for both runners; cases that justify non-empty stderr must record the justification in the case fixture entry.
output_contract_strategy.json_strategy: subset assertion against locked fields; `generated_at` is always excluded from the lock; `actual` strings that include counts or path interpolation are excluded unless explicitly listed.
output_contract_strategy.reason_code_strategy: exact literal match for stable reason_codes (e.g. lifecycle_complete, evidence_refs_resolved, in_sync, advisory_only_in_v3.5.0); prefix match for templated codes (e.g. lifecycle_missing:<kinds>, malformed_refs:<token>, waivered_until:<date>, post_baseline_new_pair_*).
output_contract_strategy.cache_strategy: test runner sets PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and asserts post-run that no __pycache__ or *.pyc files appear under the fixture repo root or under the project root that the test orchestrates.

fixture_strategy.fixture_repo_root_strategy: tests must instantiate a fully synthetic repo root containing the consilium-fabri-governance-repair-plan-v3.5.md sentinel + artifacts/governance/ + template/ so detect_repo_root() succeeds; alternatively, monkeypatch detect_repo_root to point at the fixture root.
fixture_strategy.policy_override_strategy: tests pass --policy and --baseline pointing at fixture-local copies; production policy and baseline must never be consumed by tests.
fixture_strategy.registry_override_strategy: tests pass --evidence-ref-policy pointing at fixture-local copies; controlled malformed registries live alongside the fixture and never under artifacts/governance/.
fixture_strategy.timestamp_strategy: fixtures inline deterministic Taipei ISO 8601 timestamps; runner-emitted generated_at is always excluded from the byte lock.

limitations: Coverage matrix is planning-only; no golden CLI tests are implemented in TASK-1036.
Static inspection of the runners is performed via `Read` tool only; no `Bash`-driven CLI invocation of the production runners is performed in this task.

Reason_code surface is enumerated from runner source as observed at PCACC sha=4dbb8a219093cc12 / quality sha=456b8328482b18a5; future runner edits will require reason_code surface refresh in a separate task.

Group GCLI-PRECOMMIT-EVREF case GCLI-PRECOMMIT-EVREF-002 ORC marker text is asserted by substring match; if future Evidence Ref policy registry tightens the marker into a structured heading, both the runner and this group must be re-anchored.
Group GCLI-QUALITY-IMPORT depends on subprocess hygiene of the running interpreter; future Python release behavior changes (e.g. default site-packages lookup) may require fixture updates.
Group GCLI-QUALITY-RUFF-ADVISORY locks only the advisory-only contract; lifting QC-RUFF-001 to blocking would require a separate decision and a new group.

Fixture root artifacts/verify/TASK-1037/fixtures/ is named for the next implementation lifecycle; if the TASK ID assigned to that lifecycle differs, the fixture root must be re-mapped at implementation time.

Coverage gaps and case groups are best-effort enumeration based on read-only inspection; additional reason_codes that are reachable only through unusual fixture configurations may exist and remain unenumerated.
TASK-1036 does not assert that the future implementation will pass; it only enumerates what must be locked and how.
TASK-1036 does not authorize modification of the PCACC active check surface; if a future task adds a new PCACC check, this matrix must be extended in the same lifecycle that introduces the check.
